title: Stop a glass bottle rolling off a sloped drainboard toward an open worktop edge and stand it upright on a coaster
instruction: Stop the rolling glass bottle before it goes over the edge of the worktop, then stand it upright on the cork coaster.
context: Almost everyone has lunged to catch a glass bottle knocked onto its side on a sloped kitchen drainboard as it rolls across the counter toward the floor. Unlike static pick-and-place, the bottle crosses the level worktop in under one and a half seconds: arriving late lets it drop off the open counter edge, while lunging too hard bats it off the front, back, or end. Stopping the bottle safely on the counter earns partial credit, and grasping the stopped cylinder, turning it ninety degrees cap-up without dropping it, and setting it upright inside a recessed cork coaster out of the rolling path completes the job so it cannot roll again.
setup: Station bench; coordinates in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x away from the arms, y left. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open; one fixed layout (object_jitter=0). Worktop: 38 mm laminate kitchen worktop cut-off, 52.0 cm wide (y from -23.0 to +29.0) by 36.0 cm deep (x from +14.5 to +50.5), clamped to the bench at its rear corners with two F-clamps; right end y = -23.0 cm is an open 3.8 cm drop marked with a 1.2 cm red trim strip, with a 34.0 x 16.0 x 1.0 cm charcoal foam catch pad on the bench below (y from -39.5 to -23.5). Drainboard: 36.0 x 17.0 x 1.2 cm grey melamine board, our fixture, stuck to the worktop with double-sided mounting tape at its low end and under the shim; shimmed 8.9 mm at y = +28.0 cm so it slopes 3.0 +/- 0.2 degrees down to meet the worktop flush (0 mm step) at y = +11.0 cm. Bottle: unopened VOSS Artesian Still Water 375 mL straight cylindrical glass bottle (54.0 mm diameter, 229.0 mm height, 700 g; dark grey cap toward +x), lying on its side at x = +37.5 +/- 0.3 cm on the start tape mark 14.0 cm up-slope from the y = +11.0 cm foot (y = +24.9 cm), held at rest behind a straightedge lifted straight up at t = 0.00 s. Coaster: IKEA 365+ cork coaster (art. 302.829.46; 100 mm outer diameter, 92 mm inner recess, 4.0 mm floor + 3.0 mm rim) taped to the worktop on its (20.5, -2.0) +/- 0.5 cm mark with double-sided mounting tape, 5.5 mm clear of the rolling bottle's path. Checked by tape marks, protractor, and top-camera photo.
scoring: Whole-trial zero rule (checked from the trial video; final photo and ruler confirm the end state): 0.0 permanently if the bottle's centre ever passes outside the counter footprint (x < 14.5 cm, x > 50.5 cm, y < -23.0 cm, or y > +29.0 cm) or its lowest point drops below 2.5 cm above the bench top. Otherwise, read at trial end (each non-zero level requires 1.0 s, 20 steps at 20 Hz, at rest (in the simulator linear speed < 10 mm/s and angular speed < 0.15 rad/s; on the bench, nothing moves on the video for 1 s), resting on its support (in the simulator at least 1.0 N of contact; on the bench, nothing moves on the video for 1 s), and both grippers at least 3.0 cm clear of the bottle and coaster without touching the bottle; the trial ends early once 1.0 has held 3.5 s more so the arms finish parked): 1.0 if the bottle stands upright cap-up (axis within 5.0 degrees of vertical: set square and photo) resting on the cork coaster (in the simulator at least 1.0 N of coaster contact; on the bench, nothing moves on the video for 1 s) with its base centre within 22.0 mm of the coaster centre (ruler) and the coaster still within 15.0 mm of its taped (20.5, -2.0) cm mark (the tape held); 0.5 if the bottle is resting safely on the counter with grippers clear (e.g. lying on its side or standing cap-down / outside the coaster); 0.0 if still moving or still held or within 3.0 cm of a gripper.
reset_notes: Verify the cork coaster sits flat on its taped (20.5, -2.0) cm mark, lay the unopened glass bottle cap-toward-+x against a straightedge on the 14.0 cm up-slope tape mark at x = +37.5 cm, verify against the top-camera start photo, and lift the straightedge straight up at t = 0.00 s; about 15 seconds. Nothing is opened, wet, or sticky; inspect the bottle if it dropped onto the foam catch pad and replace it if chipped.
fidelity: True-size rigid bodies; clamped worktop, 3.0 deg drainboard and cork coaster stuck down with double-sided mounting tape (our fixtures) are fixed kinematic colliders. Bottle axial inertia 0.35 m R^2, angular damping 0.05/s; contact-gated roll torque (0.035 m/s^2, >= 0.5 N counter load, reaction on the clamped counter; 0 airborne, upright, at rest); no welds. Sim: the released bottle creeps ~1.5 s before rolling. Unmodelled: slosh, fracture.
